-- [sockets table of one mount pass] = { [socketName] = { shift, pieces } } (Door.postMount)
local doorPass = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

local MESH_SLOTS_CLOSE = {
	Door = {
		-- TWO SOCKETS, ONE ITEM (2026-09-22). The cabin doorway is a DOUBLE
		-- door: two leaves, 5.76 studs apart, whose RotationParts face OPPOSITE
		-- ways (LookVector dot -0.995). It used to return one item per leaf,
		-- which meant applyMeshSlot mounted IDENTICAL pieces on both — fine for
		-- the stock planked art, which is front/back symmetric, but a themed
		-- leaf then showed its decorated face on one door and its bare back on
		-- the other (DiscoOcto's tentacle, caught in preview).
		--
		-- So the pair is now ONE item (the Doors folder) with the two leaves as
		-- separate sockets, exactly like Window's BasePart + CoverPart. A skin
		-- supplies a LeftDoor piece and a RightDoor piece.
		--
		-- The rig is deliberately NOT renamed: ShipSoundManager resolves the
		-- path string "Doors.Door.RotationPart", so both items keep the name
		-- "Door" and left/right is decided geometrically below.
		items = function(ship)
			local structure = ship:FindFirstChild("Structure")
			local f = (structure and structure:FindFirstChild("Doors"))
				or ship:FindFirstChild("Doors") -- old-tree fallback
			return f and { f } or {}
		end,
		sockets = function(folder)
			-- canonical rig 2026-07-23: RotationPart is the invisible solid
			-- door leaf on the hinge (old Collider); every visual is a
			-- DefaultMesh welded to it. Static side = the hull cabin itself.
			local leaves = {}
			for _, item in ipairs(folder:GetChildren()) do
				local rp = item:FindFirstChild("RotationPart")
				if rp then table.insert(leaves, rp) end
			end
			if #leaves == 0 then return {} end
			if #leaves == 1 then
				-- a one-leaf door: both socket names resolve to it, so a skin
				-- built for the pair still dresses it instead of failing
				return { LeftDoor = leaves[1], RightDoor = leaves[1] }
			end
			-- Which leaf is which must NEVER flip between spawns, so decide it
			-- from geometry rather than child order: project each leaf onto the
			-- hull's RightVector. Falls back to child order if the hull is gone.
			local ship = folder
			while ship and not ship:FindFirstChild("Hull") do ship = ship.Parent end
			local hull = ship and ship:FindFirstChild("Hull")
			if hull and hull:IsA("BasePart") then
				local right = hull.CFrame.RightVector
				table.sort(leaves, function(a, b)
					return a.Position:Dot(right) < b.Position:Dot(right)
				end)
			end
			return { LeftDoor = leaves[1], RightDoor = leaves[2] }
		end,
		-- SPREAD TO THE HINGES (2026-09-22). A themed leaf is usually wider
		-- than the rig's 5.30 — DiscoOcto's is 6.51, carrying its own hinge
		-- barrels — so two of them centred on sockets 5.76 apart OVERLAP in the
		-- middle of the doorway by 0.75 studs.
		--
		-- Each leaf is pushed outward by half its excess width, which restores
		-- the rig's own 0.462 gap. Derived from the mesh at mount time rather
		-- than a constant, so ANY door skin self-corrects and the designer sets
		-- nothing per theme.
		--
		-- ONE PUSH PER LEAF (2026-10-02). A leaf may carry several pieces (a
		-- see-through glass beside the leaf, sharing its pivot). Each used to be
		-- pushed by its OWN width, so the narrow glass stayed put while its leaf
		-- moved 0.61 studs: DiscoOcto's portholes lost their glass. Every piece on
		-- a socket now moves by the widest one's push. One mount pass = one
		-- `sockets` table (def.sockets(item) builds it fresh for each pass), so
		-- the pieces are remembered per table, weakly.
		postMount = function(socketName, sockets, mesh)
			local a, b = sockets.LeftDoor, sockets.RightDoor
			local socket = sockets[socketName]
			if not (a and b and socket) or a == b then return end
			local outward = socket.Position - (a.Position + b.Position) / 2
			if outward.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
			outward = outward.Unit
			-- oriented extent along the doorway axis, so rotation cannot fool it
			local function extent(p)
				local cf, sz = p.CFrame, p.Size
				return math.abs(outward:Dot(cf.RightVector)) * sz.X
					+ math.abs(outward:Dot(cf.UpVector)) * sz.Y
					+ math.abs(outward:Dot(cf.LookVector)) * sz.Z
			end
			local function push(p, by)
				p.CFrame = p.CFrame + outward * by
				-- mountMesh already welded at the OLD pose; re-seat it or physics
				-- snaps the leaf straight back to the overlap
				local w = p:FindFirstChild("AutoWeld")
				if w and w:IsA("Weld") then
					w.C0 = socket.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(p.CFrame)
				end
			end
			local pass = doorPass[sockets]
			if not pass then
				pass = {}
				doorPass[sockets] = pass
			end
			local leaf = pass[socketName]
			if not leaf then
				leaf = { shift = 0, pieces = {} }
				pass[socketName] = leaf
			end
			-- a leaf at or under rig width needs none
			local shift = math.max(leaf.shift, (extent(mesh) - extent(socket)) / 2)
			if shift > leaf.shift then
				for _, p in ipairs(leaf.pieces) do
					if p.Parent then push(p, shift - leaf.shift) end
				end
			end
			if shift > 0 then push(mesh, shift) end
			table.insert(leaf.pieces, mesh)
			leaf.shift = shift
		end,
		hideParts = function(item)
			-- NOTE: must reference MESH_SLOTS.Door (in scope), NOT
			-- MESH_SLOTS_CLOSE — a local is not visible inside its own
			-- initializer, so that resolved to nil at runtime and the
			-- thrown error killed the wiring loop for every later slot
			-- (the 10s waitForSkins stall, 2026-07-24).
			return defaultMeshesOf(MESH_SLOTS.Door.sockets(item))
		end,
	},
}
MESH_SLOTS.Door = MESH_SLOTS_CLOSE.Door
MESH_SLOTS.Window = {
	items = function(ship)
		local structure = ship:FindFirstChild("Structure")
		local windows = structure and structure:FindFirstChild("Windows")
		local out = {}
		for _, name in { "LeftSideWindow", "RightSideWindow" } do
			local m = (windows and windows:FindFirstChild(name))
				or ship:FindFirstChild(name) -- old-tree fallback
			if m then table.insert(out, m) end
		end
		return out
	end,
	sockets = function(item)
		-- BasePart = the frame; CoverPart = the swinging, cannon-breakable
		-- cover (2026-07-24) — both skinnable. Skin pieces on CoverPart
		-- ride the open/close motor and fly off with the break.
		return {
			BasePart = item:FindFirstChild("BasePart"),
			CoverPart = item:FindFirstChild("CoverPart"),
		}
	end,
	hideParts = function(item)
		return defaultMeshesOf(MESH_SLOTS.Window.sockets(item))
	end,
}
MESH_SLOTS.Board = {
	items = function(ship)
		-- the canonical Board PART is the item (ship nameplate; keeps the
		-- name "Board" — ShipNameBoardService/GameFlow/Intro find it by name)
		local b = ship:FindFirstChild("Board", true)
		return b and { b } or {}
	end,
	sockets = function(item)
		return { Board = item }
	end,
	hideParts = function(item)
		return defaultMeshesOf(MESH_SLOTS.Board.sockets(item))
	end,
}
-- BELL (2026-09-28: the Shipyard sold bell skins the Arena never wore). The sockets
-- are the three hidden rig parts Base / Rotation / Tounge (the rig's spelling, PR #25).
-- The visible art is a named MeshPart under each (BasePart / RotationPart /
-- TonguePart, on a SkinWeld), and a skin's pieces carry those same names — so the
-- socket KEY is the art's name, and the authored art hides only while its own socket
-- wears a piece. BellRing finds the parts through the Motor6D chain, not these names.
MESH_SLOTS.Bell = {
	items = function(ship)
		local props = ship:FindFirstChild("Props")
		local bell = (props and props:FindFirstChild("Bell")) or ship:FindFirstChild("Bell", true)
		return bell and { bell } or {}
	end,
	sockets = function(item)
		local out = {}
		for piece, rigName in pairs({ BasePart = "Base", RotationPart = "Rotation", TonguePart = "Tounge" }) do
			local part = item:FindFirstChild(rigName)
			if part then out[piece] = part end
		end
		return out
	end,
	hideParts = function(item)
		local out = defaultMeshesOf(MESH_SLOTS.Bell.sockets(item))
		for piece, socket in pairs(MESH_SLOTS.Bell.sockets(item)) do
			local art = socket:FindFirstChild(piece)
			if art and art:IsA("BasePart") then table.insert(out, art) end
		end
		return out
	end,
}
MESH_SLOTS.Stove = {
	items = function(ship)
		local props = ship:FindFirstChild("Props")
		local kitchen = props and props:FindFirstChild("Kitchen")
		local stove = (kitchen and kitchen:FindFirstChild("Stove")) or ship:FindFirstChild("Stove", true)
		return stove and { stove } or {}
	end,
	sockets = function(item)
		return { Stove = item } -- the Part is the socket; its DefaultMesh child is the visual
	end,
	hideParts = function(item)
		return defaultMeshesOf(MESH_SLOTS.Stove.sockets(item))
	end,
}

return {
	slots = MESH_SLOTS,
	defaultMeshesOf = defaultMeshesOf,
	anchorUp = anchorUp,
	anchorTargetCF = anchorTargetCF,
	partsFolder = partsFolder,
}
modules.ToolSkinMount:
--[[
	ToolSkinMount — dresses a Tool in a cosmetic skin, and undresses it again.

	PORTED from the Assets place (`PVP&NPC ASSETS`,
	ServerScriptService.SkinPadService, 2026-09-23). That script is the
	original and its header is the full contract; this is the same mounting
	maths with the pad-room half removed and a `clear` added, because the
	Arena picks a skin from the player's saved loadout rather than from
	whichever pad they are standing on. Keep the two in step: a correction
	discovered here belongs there too, and the reverse.

	WHAT COUNTS AS ART  Every BasePart in the Tool carrying `SkinArt = true`.
	  That is what a skin replaces, and the frame it mounts on. It is an
	  ATTRIBUTE rather than a rule about names because the tools have held
	  their art differently (in the Assets place the sword wears `Default
	  Sword` under Handle, the flintlock `gun1` beside it, the bucket three
	  UnionOperations; in the game places each wears one `DefaultArt` MeshPart
	  under Handle since 2026-10-04). The functional rig carries no
	  `SkinArt`, so a skin change can never reach combat — not the sword's
	  Blade / Crossguard / TrailSword, not the flintlock's ShootPart, not the
	  bucket's ThrowBall.

	THE ONE EXCEPTION is the bucket's `WaterVisual`, which is resized and
	moved to sit inside whatever skin is mounted. It is never destroyed or
	replaced, and its Transparency — the thing that says whether the bucket is
	full — is never written here; BucketHandler owns that and resolves the
	part exactly once at startup, so swapping in a per-skin part would leave
	its upvalue pointing at a destroyed instance.

	DO NOT DESTROY THE ART — it is hidden instead, because it is the mount
	reference and has to stay measurable. Its authored look is stashed as
	attributes ON THE PART the first time it is hidden, so `clear` can put it
	back exactly; state parked next to the Instance cannot fall out of step
	with it. (SkinPadService never needed this: a pad only ever swaps one skin
	for another and never returns to Default.)

	THE MOUNT FRAME IS RECORDED (2026-10-04)  The Default art was replaced by
	the defaults the skin plugin set up in PVP&NPC ASSETS, and the old art was
	deleted. Every skin was tuned against the OLD art's frame, so that frame is
	kept as two attributes on the Tool, measured off the old art just before it
	went: `MountGrip` (CFrame, Handle space: the old art's box centre in its own
	basis) and `MountLength` (its length along Z, for the sword's hilt slide).
	When they are present they ARE the mount reference, and the `SkinArt` parts
	(now the new Default) are only what a skin hides. Without them the frame is
	still read off the art, as before. The Assets place's tools (and so the
	ZAAL Assets plugin's preview and SkinPadService) carry the same two.
]]

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local ToolSkinMount = {}

local GRIP_PART_NAME = "Handle" -- the weld root, on every Tool
local ART_ATTRIBUTE = "SkinArt" -- marks the art a skin replaces
local SKIN_ATTRIBUTE = "SkinPart" -- marks a skin THIS module mounted

-- Fractions OF THE BUCKET'S HEIGHT, measured off the authored union bucket so
-- a fitted skin keeps its proportions: that water sits 0.185 below a rim on a
-- bucket 1.659 tall, and the column is 0.800 deep. Copied from
-- ServerStorage.SkinRoom in the Assets place, which is where they were derived.
local WATER_HEADROOM_FRAC = 0.185 / 1.659
local WATER_DEPTH_FRAC = 0.800 / 1.659

-- One row per tool. `catalog` is the folder name under ReplicatedStorage.ToolSkins
-- and the key the lobby's ToolShopService saves under; `toolName` is the Tool in
-- StarterPack, which is NOT the same string for the sword.
--
-- skinPitch / skinYaw / skinRoll are the row's DEFAULT correction, applied to
-- every skin in the folder unless the model overrides it. They describe THE
-- TOOL, not the skin: they cancel the rotation baked into the art a skin mounts
-- on. The bucket's is 90/90 because its mount basis is a Union whose own frame
-- lies on its side, so every bucket skin authored the normal way up needs the
-- same turn. The flintlocks carry their own SkinYaw (-90) per model.
ToolSkinMount.TOOLS = {
	{ catalog = "Sword", toolName = "sword", attribute = "SwordSkin", alignHilt = true },
	{ catalog = "Flintlock", toolName = "Flintlock", attribute = "FlintlockSkin" },
	{ catalog = "Bucket", toolName = "Bucket", attribute = "BucketSkin",
		water = "WaterVisual", skinPitch = 90, skinRoll = 90 },
}

function ToolSkinMount.configFor(catalogName)
	for _, config in ipairs(ToolSkinMount.TOOLS) do
		if config.catalog == catalogName then
			return config
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- the MeshPart a catalog Model / MeshPart wears: the entry itself, or the first one in it
-- (the ZAAL Assets plugin's preview mounts the skin model this way; it has no ToolSkinRows)
function ToolSkinMount.meshOf(entry)
	if typeof(entry) ~= "Instance" then
		return nil
	end
	if entry:IsA("MeshPart") then
		return entry
	end
	return entry:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("MeshPart", true)
end


--============================================================ the art =====

local function artParts(tool)
	local parts = {}
	for _, d in ipairs(tool:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") and d:GetAttribute(ART_ATTRIBUTE) then
			table.insert(parts, d)
		end
	end
	return parts
end

-- No cache, by design. The art is only ever hidden, so the mount frame can be
-- read off it fresh on every swap and there is no stale state to lose.
--
-- THE BASIS MUST NOT DEPEND ON GetDescendants() ORDER. That order is not stable
-- across a Clone, and the Tool a player holds IS a clone of the StarterPack
-- one: in the template the bucket's body came first, in the clone the thin bail
-- did, so the mount frame silently moved to a part lying on its side and every
-- bucket skin equipped 90 degrees out. Biggest part wins, ties broken by
-- position, so the same part is chosen from any order. For a single-art tool —
-- the sword, the flintlock — there is only one part, so this still resolves to
-- exactly that part's own frame, which is what those two rely on.
local function mountReference(tool, handle)
	local parts = artParts(tool)
	-- the recorded frame of the art the skins were tuned on (see the header)
	local recorded = tool:GetAttribute("MountGrip")
	if typeof(recorded) == "CFrame" then
		return {
			parts = parts,
			grip = recorded,
			length = tool:GetAttribute("MountLength") or 0,
			hiltEnd = tool:GetAttribute("AuthoredHiltEnd") or "-Z",
		}
	end
	if #parts == 0 then
		return nil
	end

	table.sort(parts, function(a, b)
		local va = a.Size.X * a.Size.Y * a.Size.Z
		local vb = b.Size.X * b.Size.Y * b.Size.Z
		if math.abs(va - vb) > 1e-6 then
			return va > vb
		end
		local pa, pb = a.Position, b.Position
		if pa.X ~= pb.X then return pa.X < pb.X end
		if pa.Y ~= pb.Y then return pa.Y < pb.Y end
		return pa.Z < pb.Z
	end)

	local basis = parts[1].CFrame
	local min = Vector3.new(math.huge, math.huge, math.huge)
	local max = -min
	for _, part in ipairs(parts) do
		local rel = basis:ToObjectSpace(part.CFrame)
		local h = part.Size / 2
		for x = -1, 1, 2 do
			for y = -1, 1, 2 do
				for z = -1, 1, 2 do
					local corner = (rel * CFrame.new(h.X * x, h.Y * y, h.Z * z)).Position
					min = min:Min(corner)
					max = max:Max(corner)
				end
			end
		end
	end

	return {
		parts = parts,
		grip = handle.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(basis * CFrame.new((min + max) / 2)),
		length = (max - min).Z,
		hiltEnd = tool:GetAttribute("AuthoredHiltEnd") or "-Z",
	}
end

local function hideArt(part)
	if part:GetAttribute("AuthoredTransparency") == nil then
		part:SetAttribute("AuthoredTransparency", part.Transparency)
		part:SetAttribute("AuthoredCanCollide", part.CanCollide)
		part:SetAttribute("AuthoredCanQuery", part.CanQuery)
		part:SetAttribute("AuthoredCanTouch", part.CanTouch)
		part:SetAttribute("AuthoredMassless", part.Massless)
	end
	part.Transparency = 1
	part.CanCollide = false
	part.CanQuery = false
	part.CanTouch = false
	part.Massless = true
end

local function showArt(part)
	local transparency = part:GetAttribute("AuthoredTransparency")
	if transparency == nil then
		return -- never hidden, so nothing to restore
	end
	part.Transparency = transparency
	part.CanCollide = part:GetAttribute("AuthoredCanCollide") == true
	part.CanQuery = part:GetAttribute("AuthoredCanQuery") == true
	part.CanTouch = part:GetAttribute("AuthoredCanTouch") == true
	part.Massless = part:GetAttribute("AuthoredMassless") == true
end

--=========================================================== the water =====

-- Sit the tool's water inside the skin that was just mounted, or put it back
-- where it was authored when there is no skin (`skin` nil) or the skin's
-- interior was never measured.
--
-- The water is held by a Weld created ONCE and afterwards only retuned. The
-- obvious version — drop the weld, move the part, weld it again — churns the
-- player's own physics assembly on every skin change: for that moment the water
-- is a loose body inside the character, and rebuilding an assembly under
-- someone who is walking is what makes them snap and lose control for a beat. A
-- Weld carries its offset in C0, so nothing is ever detached. (A WeldConstraint
-- cannot do this: it has no offset.)
local function fitWater(config, handle, model, skin)
	if not config.water then
		return
	end
	local water = handle:FindFirstChild(config.water)
	if not water or not water:IsA("BasePart") then
		return
	end

	if water:GetAttribute("AuthoredSize") == nil then
		water:SetAttribute("AuthoredSize", water.Size)
		water:SetAttribute("AuthoredGrip", handle.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(water.CFrame))
	end

	local size, grip
	local diameter = model and model:GetAttribute("WaterDiameter")
	local rim = model and model:GetAttribute("WaterRim")
	if skin and diameter and rim then
		local height = skin.Size.Y
		local depth = WATER_DEPTH_FRAC * height
		-- In the skin's own space: +Y is up (that is what the pitch/roll are
		-- for) and the origin is the centre of its bounding box, so the base of
		-- the bucket sits at -height/2 and the rim that far above it.
		local top = -height / 2 + rim - WATER_HEADROOM_FRAC * height
		-- WaterOffset moves the column within the skin, in the SKIN'S OWN
		-- space. It exists because everything above is measured from the
		-- mesh's BOUNDING BOX, and a box is only centred on the bucket when
		-- the bucket is the widest thing in the mesh: hang a large accessory
		-- off one side and the box centre shifts toward it while the bucket
		-- does not.
		local offset = model:GetAttribute("WaterOffset") or Vector3.zero
		-- X is the cylinder's axis, Y its diameter. Z is written equal to Y
		-- only so the bounding box stops overstating the width.
		size = Vector3.new(depth, diameter, diameter)
		-- Turned a quarter about Z so the cylinder's axis lies along the skin's
		-- up axis, and centred on the skin's own axis of revolution.
		grip = handle.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(skin.CFrame
			* CFrame.new(offset.X, top - depth / 2 + offset.Y, offset.Z)
			* CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.pi / 2))
	else
		size = water:GetAttribute("AuthoredSize")
		grip = water:GetAttribute("AuthoredGrip")
	end

	local weld = water:FindFirstChild("WaterFitWeld")
	if not weld then
		weld = Instance.new("Weld")
		weld.Name = "WaterFitWeld"
		weld.Part0 = handle
		weld.Part1 = water
		weld.C0 = handle.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(water.CFrame)
		weld.Parent = water
		-- Only now that the Weld has hold of it can the authored
		-- WeldConstraint go — two constraints on one pair fight each other.
		for _, child in ipairs(water:GetChildren()) do
			if child:IsA("WeldConstraint") then
				child:Destroy()
			end
		end
	end
	-- Writes that change nothing are skipped, so re-dressing cannot resize a
	-- part inside the character over and over.
	if (water.Size - size).Magnitude > 1e-4 then
		water.Size = size
	end
	weld.C0 = grip
end

--========================================================== mount/clear =====

local function removeMounted(handle)
	for _, child in ipairs(handle:GetChildren()) do
		if child:GetAttribute(SKIN_ATTRIBUTE) then
			child:Destroy()
		end
	end
end

-- Back to the tool's own art: drop the mounted skin, show the art again, and
-- return the water to the size and place it was authored at.
function ToolSkinMount.clear(tool)
	local handle = tool:FindFirstChild(GRIP_PART_NAME)
	if not handle or not handle:IsA("BasePart") then
		return false
	end
	local config = nil
	for _, row in ipairs(ToolSkinMount.TOOLS) do
		if row.toolName == tool.Name then config = row end
	end
	removeMounted(handle)
	for _, part in ipairs(artParts(tool)) do
		showArt(part)
	end
	if config then
		fitWater(config, handle, nil, nil)
	end
	tool:SetAttribute("SkinApplied", nil)
	return true
end

-- Dress `tool` in `model`, a catalog entry (a ToolSkinRows entry: it answers .Name and
-- :GetAttribute), wearing `mesh` — a fresh MeshPart of it this function now owns
-- (ToolSkinRows.newMesh). Without `mesh`, a copy of the entry's own MeshPart is worn
-- (meshOf — the plugin's preview). Returns true when something was mounted.
function ToolSkinMount.apply(config, tool, model, mesh)
	if not mesh then
		local template = ToolSkinMount.meshOf(model)
		if not template then
			warn("[ToolSkinMount] " .. tostring(model.Name) .. " has no MeshPart in it; "
				.. "leaving " .. tool:GetFullName() .. " as it is.")
			return false
		end
		mesh = template:Clone()
	end
	local handle = tool:FindFirstChild(GRIP_PART_NAME)
	if not handle or not handle:IsA("BasePart") then
		warn("[ToolSkinMount] no BasePart named '" .. GRIP_PART_NAME .. "' in "
			.. tool:GetFullName() .. "; cannot mount a skin.")
		mesh:Destroy()
		return false
	end

	-- Re-read every time; the art is hidden below, never destroyed.
	local reference = mountReference(tool, handle)
	if not reference then
		warn("[ToolSkinMount] nothing in " .. tool:GetFullName() .. " is marked "
			.. ART_ATTRIBUTE .. ", so there is no frame to mount a skin on.")
		mesh:Destroy()
		return false
	end

	removeMounted(handle)

	mesh.Name = config.toolName .. "Skin"
	mesh:SetAttribute(SKIN_ATTRIBUTE, true)
	-- A skin made by DUPLICATING the tool's own art arrives carrying SkinArt.
	-- Left on, the skin counts as art: it is hidden the instant it is mounted,
	-- and folded into the mount box of every later swap.
	mesh:SetAttribute(ART_ATTRIBUTE, nil)
	-- Clone copies CollectionService tags, and a catalog entry that is a bare
	-- MeshPart carries its row's tag ITSELF. A tagged skin in someone's hand is
	-- read by the Assets place's room builder as a display waiting to be placed
	-- and reparented into the row WHILE IT IS WELDED TO THE PLAYER, which drags
	-- the character across the map. What is in a hand is not a display.
	for _, tag in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTags(mesh)) do
		CollectionService:RemoveTag(mesh, tag)
	end
	-- Joints that came along with the art can only do harm; this mesh gets its
	-- own below. Anything else it brings — a SurfaceAppearance, say — is what
	-- makes it look right, so only joints are removed.
	for _, child in ipairs(mesh:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("JointInstance") or child:IsA("WeldConstraint") then
			child:Destroy()
		end
	end
	-- The catalog models are saved colliding and massy; a colliding, weighty
	-- part welded to the Handle would drag the character around.
	mesh.Anchored = false
	mesh.CanCollide = false
	mesh.CanQuery = false
	mesh.CanTouch = false
	mesh.Massless = true

	local frame = reference.grip

	if config.alignHilt then
		-- Sword meshes are not authored to one convention: some carry the hilt
		-- at local -Z (like the Tool's own sword) and some at +Z. Flip
		-- end-for-end about Y when they disagree, so the blade stays in its own
		-- plane and the cutting edge keeps pointing the authored way.
		local hiltEnd = model:GetAttribute("HiltEnd")
		if hiltEnd and hiltEnd ~= reference.hiltEnd then
			frame = frame * CFrame.Angles(0, math.pi, 0)
		end
		-- Slide so the HILT stays in the fist whatever the blade's length is.
		frame = frame * CFrame.new(0, 0, (mesh.Size.Z - reference.length) / 2)
	end

	-- Hand corrections: the model's own attribute first, then the row default.
	-- A skin needs no attribute at all when it follows its folder's convention.
	local pitch = model:GetAttribute("SkinPitch") or config.skinPitch
	local yaw = model:GetAttribute("SkinYaw") or config.skinYaw
	local roll = model:GetAttribute("SkinRoll") or config.skinRoll
	if pitch or yaw or roll then
		frame = frame * CFrame.Angles(math.rad(pitch or 0), math.rad(yaw or 0), math.rad(roll or 0))
	end

	-- Positional nudge, in HANDLE space: +Y is up out of the fist, +Z forward.
	-- Applied after the rotations so the two are independent.
	local offset = model:GetAttribute("SkinOffset")
	if offset then
		frame = CFrame.new(offset) * frame
	end

	mesh.CFrame = handle.CFrame * frame

	local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
	weld.Name = "SkinWeld"
	weld.Part0 = handle
	weld.Part1 = mesh
	weld.Parent = mesh
	mesh.Parent = handle

	-- After the mesh is placed, so the water is measured against where the skin
	-- actually landed rather than where it was about to land.
	fitWater(config, handle, model, mesh)

	-- The list was measured BEFORE the skin was mounted, so a skin can never
	-- end up hiding itself.
	for _, part in ipairs(reference.parts) do
		hideArt(part)
	end

	tool:SetAttribute("SkinApplied", model.Name)
	return true
end

return ToolSkinMount
